parsed.explanation: The family F_k={x_0,...,x_k,y_k} (all symbols distinct) is nonempty, consists of nonempty finite sets, and is pairwise intersecting (all share x_0), so it satisfies the lemma's hypotheses. Each T_n={y_0,...,y_{n-1},x_n} is a finite transversal: it meets F_i via y_i for i<n and via x_n for i>=n; deleting y_i kills the intersection with F_i, deleting x_n kills it with F_n, so each T_n is inclusion-minimal, and the T_n are pairwise distinct. If transversals formed the up-set of finitely many B_j, each B_j would itself be a transversal, forcing every minimal transversal to equal some B_j -- impossible. The write-up's induction actually fails: the reduction to (F_c, C\{c}) characterizes only transversals meeting C\{c}, which need not contain a family member. Since B_j, b_j, L, T all rest on this lemma, the finiteness obligation and the whole proof are invalid.
